joshua.5.p1.b1.text: Now when all the Amorite kings west of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings along the coast heard how the LORD had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the Israelites … their hearts melted and their spirits failed for fear of the Israelites.

joshua.5.p1.b2.text: “Make flint knives and circumcise the sons of Israel once again.”

joshua.5.p1.b3.text: So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the sons of Israel at Gibeath-haaraloth.

joshua.5.p2.b1.text: All those who came out of Egypt—all the men of war—had died on the journey in the wilderness after they had left Egypt.

joshua.5.p2.b2.text: And Joshua raised up their sons in their place, and these were the ones he circumcised.

joshua.5.p2.b3.text: And after all the nation had been circumcised, they stayed there in the camp until they were healed.

joshua.5.p2.b4.text: “Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you.”

joshua.5.p3.b1.text: On the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, while the Israelites were camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho, they kept the Passover.

joshua.5.p3.b2.text: The day after the Passover, on that very day, they ate unleavened bread and roasted grain from the produce of the land.

joshua.5.p3.b3.text: And the day after they had eaten from the produce of the land, the manna ceased. There was no more manna for the Israelites, so that year they began to eat the crops of the land of Canaan.

joshua.5.p4.b1.text: Now when Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a drawn sword in His hand.

joshua.5.p4.b2.text: “Are You for us or for our enemies?”

joshua.5.p4.b3.text: “Neither,” … “I have now come as Commander of the LORD’s army.”

joshua.5.p4.b4.text: “What does my Lord have to say to His servant?”

joshua.5.p5.b1.text: “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy.”
